reason: The cited evidence directly supports all key premises: E3 confirms Zr increases atomic size difference and solid solution strengthening; E1 and E2 show hot rolling plus cold rolling and annealing improves ductility and retains BCC structure; E1 reports density ~5 g/cm³ and identifies Ti65(AlCrNbV)28Zr7 as optimum. However, the hypothesis overstates the evidence by claiming a 20–30% high-temperature yield strength improvement, whereas the cited passages only report room-temperature tensile properties and do not provide high-temperature mechanical data.
premises: Zr addition increases atomic size difference and solid solution strengthening in Ti65(AlCrNbV)35
Hot rolling + cold rolling + rapid annealing refines microstructure and improves ductility
Zr-containing alloys retain single BCC structure after thermomechanical treatment
Density of Zr-added alloys remains low (~5 g/cm³)
Ti65(AlCrNbV)28Zr7 exhibits optimum mechanical properties among tested compositions
